title: line
content_html:
line

A line can divide a surface, carry the eye across it, record where a hand went or give a voice a place to pause. The curves in curve machine or curve poems and the arranged lines of all the little cracks give the eye different paths to follow. A line can also become a route, a sentence or part of a diagram. Its beginning and end may matter as much as the path it takes, especially when it leaves a connection for the reader to continue. Curve machine · all the little cracks

Reading note. Daoism. Chapter 27 of the Daodejing describes a skilled traveller who leaves no tracks. A line in curve poems can suggest a journey even when the route by which it was made is impossible to reconstruct. Where does the eye travel when the original movement is unavailable to it? Daodejing, 27 · Tao and Art in the Library
